representation: Unit circle of radius 1 on the left with a horizontal height-connector carrying the point's y-coordinate to a vertical sine axis on the right; the sine value is shown as a signed height, not as a curve trace.
entities: radius line from centre to the moving point
horizontal connector from the point to the sine axis
vertical sine axis with +1 and -1 ticks
sine bar from the axis baseline to the sine dot
motion: theta = angle + 0.5236*t, so one full revolution per 12 s; the point, radius, connector, bar and sine dot are all driven by the same theta expression. A small radius pulse on the moving point marks each quarter turn.
controls: slider 'angle' 0..6.2 rad sets the starting angle of the sweep (keyboard operable)
checkpoints: 0.1 s: theta = 0, height 0, connector at the baseline
3 s: quarter turn, height = 1 at the upper tick, x = 0
6 s: half turn, height 0 while x = -1
11.9 s: full turn, sin 2pi = sin 0, period 2pi
misconceptionTest: Checkpoint 3 shows the point at x = -1 with height 0 (sine is not the x-coordinate). Checkpoint 2 states height = 1 while x = 0, and the connector length always equals |sin theta|, so sine is shown as a circular-motion height, not only a triangle ratio.
accessibility: Alt text names every element and the height relationship; slider is keyboard operable; heights are labelled with ticks and text, not colour; reducedMotion no-autoplay.
